earlier_scan.note: Extinct, unclassifiable Tanzanian variety; Glottolog lists zero references.

sources.citation: Moser, Rupert. 2003. Die Bedeutung von mündlichen Überlieferungen für die Historie: Oraltraditionen und Schriftquellen über eine afrikanische Völkerwanderung. In Peter Rusterholz & Rupert Moser (Hg.), Wir sind Erinnerung. Bern/Stuttgart/Wien: Paul Haupt. [read in the full-text republication on the author's homepage moserrupert.heimat.eu, Internet Archive copy 2022-04-01; the same page also carries Moser 2001 'Geschlechterbeziehungen bei den mutterrechtlichen Mwera von Südtanzania' (in A. Tunis (Hg.), Faszination der Kulturen, Berlin: Reimer), which names the Hamba only as western neighbours of the Mwera]
sources.note: No phonology and no linguistic data of any kind on Hamba. Relevant content (verbatim): '..vermischten sich.. zu einem Teil mit den wildbeuterischen Hamba, die möglicherweise im heutigen Siedlungsgebiet der Mwera gelebt hatten und von diesen - soweit nicht assimiliert - nach Nordwesten abgedrängt worden waren. So leben nördlich der Mwera heute Matumbi, nordwestlich Ndonde und einige wenige bis vor kurzem noch jägerische Hamba-Ndonde und Hamba.'.. 'Von Umsiedlungen wurden die Hamba während der britischen Kolonialzeit betroffen. Sie mussten Plantagen weichen und sind heute als eigenständige Grup…

sources.citation: Glottolog languoid record hamb1239 (hid NOCODE_Hamba; family Unclassifiable; AES extinct; Glottolog's most extensive description list = Batibo 1992, Crosse-Upcott 1956; zero descriptive refs).

Gulliver, P. H. 1959. A Tribal Map of Tanganyika. Tanganyika Notes and Records 52: 61-74 (with map; Hamba discussed p. 62 and listed in tribal note (vii) and the index as part of map group 42 'Ngindo').
sources.note: No phonology content. Relevant text (scanned, p. 62): 'In the Southern Province, for example, there is a group of people whom I have termed "Ngindo" on the map. There are distinct sub-groups such as the Ngindo proper, Ndonde, Magingo, Hamba and others.. it seems preferable to assert the genuine, close similarity and the general, underlying, common culture, language, etc., and therefore to classify the two together with some others as "Ngindo"'; tribal note (vii): 'NGINDO is the recognised, overall name for the NGINDO PROPER together with the NDONDE (east of middle Mbenkuru river), MAGINGO and…

sources.citation: Crosse-Upcott, A.R.W. 1956. The social structure of the KiNgindo-speaking peoples. PhD thesis, University of Cape Town (709-page OpenUCT scan with scanned layer; incl. Part 'Internal variations of Ngindoland', pp. 348-360 = Glottolog hh:608174, the item Glottolog ties to hamb1239 'Proto-Hamba').
sources.note: Nothing on Hamba speech at all: p. 354 (p. 417, verified on page scan) 'There is no knowing whether or not the aboriginal Hamba or Ikemba spoke kiNgindo.. Present Hamba and Ikemba speech is scarcely distinguishable from kiMagingo.' No Hamba wordlist or linguistic data anywhere (Appendix B 'Neo-Hamba' column = kiNdonde speakers of Kilimarondo, a different group). The thesis's only accent remark (p. 26, p. 30: Ngindo 'accentuating the first syllable of the stem, as opposed to the penultimate') is about kiNgindo (ngin1244), not an anterior Hamba language.
Page concerns only the Congolese Hamba (Tetela cluster, ISO hba); nothing on the Tanzanian Hamba.
